introduction.definition: A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy, E = ½·I·ω². Coefficient of speed fluctuation sets size

classification.type: Spoked cast-iron flywheel on a crank press

introduction.summary: A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy (E = ½ I ω²). In this crank press the motor slowly keeps the flywheel spinning; when the punch strikes, the flywheel gives up some energy and slows down a little, delivering a much larger peak power than the motor alone could. Between strokes the motor brings it back up to speed. Flywheels also smooth the uneven torque of engines.

foundation: Mount driver and driven machines on a rigid common base so centre distances and alignment stay fixed.
alignment: Align shafts parallel and the wheels/hubs in the same plane (straight-edge or laser); misalignment is the main cause of early wear.
piping: Fit guards that fully enclose moving parts but allow inspection and lubrication.
commissioning: Check rotation, set tension/slack or torque setting, run in and re-check after the first hours of operation.

overhaul.task: NDT of rim and spokes for cracks.

lubrication: Grease or oil the main bearings per schedule.

video_tutorials.title: Flywheel Assembly — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Flywheel Assembly.
A flywheel is a heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy, E = ½·I·ω².
It smooths fluctuating torque and supplies short bursts of high power — in a crank press it slows slightly at each stroke, giving up energy, and the motor brings it back up to speed between strokes.
Typical applications include mechanical presses and punches; reciprocating engines and compressors; energy storage (high-speed composite flywheels); rolling mills, shears.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Flywheel: Rim, Spokes, Hub & Key (stores kinetic energy), Shaft, Crank Disc & Crank Pin.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Flywheel Assembly — Operation

script.narration: How the Flywheel Assembly works.
The motor drives the flywheel to full speed.
The flywheel stores energy in its heavy rim.
At each stroke, the crank and rod push the ram — the flywheel slows a little and releases energy.
The ram punches the workpiece with a peak power far above the motor rating.
Between strokes the motor restores the speed.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Flywheel Assembly — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Flywheel Assembly.
Check vibration and bearing temperature.
Check key and hub tightness.
NDT of rim and spokes for cracks.
Watch for loose flywheel on shaft: knocking, fretting. Common cause: worn key/keyway.
Watch for cracked rim/spokes: vibration, visible cracks. Common cause: fatigue, overspeed.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
